decisions.decision: Gate component counts in descriptions, not entry-to-manifest equality.
decisions.rationale: PR #2187 is a real cited decision that counts do not belong in these strings. Equality is not: upstream permits an entry to carry independent catalog metadata, 'strict: false' entries need no plugin.json, and no commit in this repo's history ever had all pairs in agreement.
decisions.impact: The gate blocks the defect that actually occurred and stays silent on the taste question nobody decided. It cannot fail a marketplace that is valid upstream.

decisions.decision: Rebuild rather than patch after the round-2 BLOCKING finding.
decisions.rationale: Five of the six MAJOR findings existed only because the design resolved marketplace sources to directories. Removing that need makes them unreachable instead of fixed.
decisions.impact: The gate is 84 lines smaller and has no path handling built from marketplace input.

decisions.decision: Close #3645 with evidence instead of shipping a duplicate fix.
decisions.rationale: PR #3559 had already repaired the Copilot description on main.
decisions.impact: One issue closed with a byte-level citation; no redundant hunk in this PR.

decisions.decision: Narrow the component nouns to real manifest categories, then loosen everything else
decisions.rationale: The pattern was simultaneously too narrow and too wide: it missed '1 agent' and '3 MCP servers' while failing on 'two workflows'. Both faults share a cause. A noun list containing prose words like rules and workflows forces every other part of the pattern to stay tight to compensate. Cutting the list to categories the schema declares removes the pressure, so singular forms, hyphens and a wider window become safe.
decisions.impact: Ten counted phrasings that previously shipped are now caught, and two prose phrasings that previously failed now pass.

decisions.decision: Write test expectations out rather than derive them from the module
decisions.rationale: A test that reads its expected values from the code under test cannot detect a deletion from that code, because the deletion removes the case as well. Dropping a count token survived the whole suite for exactly this reason.
decisions.impact: Deleting any count token or component category now fails a named assertion.

patterns.pattern: Send the adversarial reviewer at the premise, not only the implementation.
patterns.context: Round 1 attacked the code and found seven real defects. Round 2 was told explicitly to attack the justification, and that is the round that found the design was wrong.
patterns.application: When a change adds a blocking gate, one review round must be aimed at whether the invariant is real, separately from whether the code implements it correctly.

patterns.pattern: Verify a reviewer's factual claim before acting on it, in both directions.
patterns.context: The reviewer's version numbers were stale and recomputing them was necessary. Its claim about PR #3559 was correct and checking it killed my own argument.
patterns.application: Re-derive every load-bearing claim from a primary source. A reviewer being wrong once is not evidence it is wrong again.

patterns.pattern: Removing a capability can delete a class of defects instead of patching them.
patterns.context: Path traversal, pluginRoot joins, containment, and strict-mode handling all existed only to resolve an entry to a directory. The narrower gate needs no path at all.
patterns.application: When review returns several findings clustered in one subsystem, ask whether the subsystem is required before fixing each finding.

patterns.pattern: Mutation testing finds untested boundaries, not just untested branches.
patterns.context: Widening the regex window from two intervening words to nine broke no test, so the boundary was decorative until a three-word case pinned it.
patterns.application: Mutate numeric bounds and thresholds, not only control flow.

patterns.pattern: Reproduce every adversarial finding locally before accepting or rejecting it
patterns.context: A third-round review returned seven findings against a redesign.
patterns.application: Each was run as a direct probe first. All seven reproduced, and one of them turned out to understate the problem: verifying its historical claim showed my own correction was wrong too.

avoidances.antipattern: Treating a convergent later fix as independent corroboration.
avoidances.consequence: PR #3559 looked like a second author reaching the same conclusion. Its branch already carried the string before it started; the merge restored pre-existing text.
avoidances.correction: Before citing convergence, check the branch base. git show <first-commit>^:<path> shows whether the value was derived or inherited.

avoidances.antipattern: Reasoning from textual similarity to intent.
avoidances.consequence: Two descriptions being the same sentence was read as proof that equality was intended. It only showed one copy had a count that the other did not.
avoidances.correction: Similarity supports the narrow claim about the differing token. Promoting it to a general invariant needs a decision record or an upstream requirement.

avoidances.antipattern: Claiming a lint ran when its config excluded every file in scope.
avoidances.consequence: The first draft of this log said scoped markdownlint reported no findings. It had reported zero files, because the config excludes .serena/**.
avoidances.correction: Read the tool's file count, not just its exit code, before writing evidence.

avoidances.antipattern: Deriving a test's expected values from the module the test constrains
avoidances.consequence: The assertion cannot fail on deletion. Removing a token from the vocabulary also removed the case that exercised it, so the mutation passed 65 tests.
avoidances.correction: Write the expected set out in the test and assert the module's set equals it, so drift in either direction is a named failure.

avoidances.antipattern: Correcting a claim a reviewer flagged without re-deriving it from the source
avoidances.consequence: The reviewer was right that 'the pairs never agreed' was false; the replacement claim was also false. The pairs agreed at four commits, which the corrected sentence still denied.
avoidances.correction: Re-run the query. The verified answer was more useful than either version: agreement existed only while both copies carried a count, so equality and countlessness are in tension and #2187 chose countlessness.

avoidances.antipattern: Treating a hardcoded file list in a gate as complete because it is complete today
avoidances.consequence: The gate would miss a sixth manifest exactly as #2187 missed the third, which is the failure it exists to prevent.
avoidances.correction: Add a test that discovers the files independently and fails when the configured list does not cover them.
